title: The rupee in 2026: a record slide, then a rebound
dek: From near 89 to the dollar in January to a record low near 96.90, then a rebound in November. What moved the rupee this year.
seoTitle: Rupee vs dollar 2026: record lows and the rebound
bigLabel: Rupees per US dollar at the close on 20 Nov (provisional, PTI), from a record low near 96.90

glance.what: The rupee hit a string of record lows in 2026, bottoming near 96.90 per dollar. It recovered to 93.70 on 9 November, eased to 94.19 by 13 November, then strengthened for several days in a row. On 20 November it crossed 93 for the first time since April and closed at 92.67 (provisional), a seven-month high.
glance.why: A weaker rupee makes imports like oil, electronics and foreign travel or education more expensive, and adds to inflation.
glance.next: Falling oil prices, foreign inflows and RBI dollar sales have helped. A stronger dollar on US rate-rise bets, or a renewed oil spike, would push the other way.

forYou: Anything priced in dollars costs more: foreign trips, overseas tuition, imported gadgets. Families receiving money from abroad get more rupees per dollar or dirham.
next: Watch oil prices and foreign investor flows.

events.title: First record low of the year
events.summary: The rupee weakens toward 91.7 per dollar as foreign investors sell Indian stocks.

events.title: Past 92 as war in West Asia lifts oil
events.summary: Soaring oil prices and fighting in the Gulf push the rupee past 92 for the first time.

events.title: A lifetime low of 93.96
events.summary: Global uncertainty drives the rupee to a new record.

events.title: Through 96 as oil surges
events.summary: The rupee hits 96.25 in early trade after closing below 96 for the first time the previous Friday. Foreign investors pulled nearly $20 billion from Indian equities in the first four months of 2026.

events.title: Hovering near record lows ahead of the RBI decision
events.summary: The rupee trades around 96.4 per dollar. The RBI keeps selling dollars to slow the fall, and markets price in a rate hike.

events.title: RBI steps in; the rupee turns
events.summary: After the RBI sells dollars and tightens currency rules, the rupee rises nearly 1% in October, one of Asia's best performers that month, and settles around 94.46 on 5 November.

events.title: A six-month high of 93.70
events.summary: The rupee touches 93.70 per dollar in early trade, its strongest in about six months, as crude falls and foreign money flows back in. It has recovered more than 3% from its record low near 96.90, and closes the day at 93.93.

events.title: A small pullback from the high
events.summary: The rupee slips 41 paise to close at 94.12 on 12 November as the dollar strengthens, then edges up to 94.05 in early trade on 13 November on foreign inflows and softer oil. One forex adviser still sees the broader trend favouring the rupee.

events.title: Slips to 94.20 on US rate worries
events.summary: The rupee falls 8 paise to close at 94.20 per dollar (provisional). Dealers point to a stronger dollar after higher-than-expected US inflation data, which raised bets that the US Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December, and to falling Indian shares.

events.title: Edges up to 94.13 as oil eases
events.summary: The rupee rises 6 paise to 94.13 per dollar in early trade on Monday, after closing Friday at 94.19 (final figure). Forex traders credit lower crude oil prices and rising Indian shares, while a strong dollar, rising US bond yields and US-Iran tension limit the gain.

events.title: Rises to 93.63 as oil falls and foreign money flows in
events.summary: The rupee closed Monday 25 paise stronger at 93.94 per dollar, then opened at 93.72 on Tuesday and touched 93.63 in early trade, PTI reports. Dealers credit lower oil prices, which ease India's import bill, and foreign investors buying Indian shares: they bought ₹4,864.68 crore of shares on Monday alone, according to exchange data. Moneycontrol links the inflows to investors moving money away from AI-linked trades elsewhere.
events.differs: Moneycontrol gives Monday's close as 93.93 and Tuesday's opening as 93.73; PTI gives 93.94 and 93.72.

events.title: Rupee crosses 93 and closes at a seven-month high of 92.67
events.summary: The rupee closed at 92.67 per dollar on Friday (provisional), 65 paise stronger than Thursday and its strongest level in seven months, PTI reports. During the day it crossed 93 for the first time since 20 April, per Business Today. Dealers credit foreign investors buying Indian shares, lower oil prices (Brent fell 1.82% to $90.31 during the day, per PTI) and a rally in Indian stocks. Business Today says foreign investors have put about $12 billion into Indian shares this month, and also points to exporters selling dollars and possible RBI action. On the two days before, PTI reported closes of 93.44 (provisional) on Wednesday and 93.32 on Thursday.
events.differs: NewsBytes gives 92.68 for Friday. PTI's own report gives the gain as both 65 and 67 paise. For Thursday, PTI gives a close of 93.32; Kotak Neo gives 93.29 in one place and 93.32 in another. For the 17 Nov close, Business Today gives 93.47.
